beats.care: Where you're allowed to protest shapes whether leaders hear you. Today's hearings could set rules for protests by students and everyone else.
beats.what: Delhi Police removed Jantar Mantar from its list of approved protest sites. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground replace it.
beats.why: A Home Ministry committee recommended other venues. It comes amid days of protests demanding the Chief Election Commissioner quit over the voter-list re-check.

cards.body: Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar's order changes a 2022 standing order, and a detailed rulebook for the new grounds will come separately. Separately, student body NSUI has asked the High Court for a probe into alleged assaults on protesters on 10 October.

a.body: The change follows a Home Ministry committee's recommendation to find alternative venues where citizens can exercise their right to protest.
a.label: Police and government say

b.body: Peaceful protest is being shut out. A lawyer told the High Court no proper alternative site was earmarked. Congress says it will go to the Supreme Court.
b.label: Opposition and petitioners say

cards.body: Yes. Article 19 of the Constitution protects peaceful assembly without arms. The state can put reasonable limits for public order, and courts decide when a limit goes too far.
cards.title: is protest a right in india?

cards.body: Jantar Mantar is actually an 18th-century observatory. Its giant stone instruments were built to track the sun, moon and stars.

cards.why: A protest near Parliament is hard to miss; critics say far-off grounds make protests easier to ignore.

hook: Delhi's famous protest spot is *off the list*. Where can people go now?

learn.t: Jantar Mantar has been Delhi's main protest spot for about two decades, from Anna Hazare's 2011 fast to the wrestlers in 2023.
